bundle.text:
# dsh-multiagents bundle patch — Phase 9 wiring.
#
# This file is the `dsh.bundle.patch` of @dh-multiagents/bundle (root
# package.json). Layer order (bottom → top):
#   1. `@deepseek-ai/dsh-base` bundle patch (first in dsh.profile.bundles)
#   2. THIS bundle patch
#   3. profile cordis.patch.yml → $DSH_HOME/cordis.patch.yml → --patch → telemetry/preset-root overlays
#
# A patch REPLACES a targeted row's WHOLE `config` (no deep-merge), so every
# row overridden below restates every key it owns. `!!js` expressions are
# evaluated in `config`/`disabled` fields (globals: process, injected
# ctx.<service>, dshHomePath(...), baseUrl).

# ── base layering (rows dsh-base already inserts; restated here so the      ──
#    dh-multiagents deployment states its intent explicitly) ──────────────────

# The native DeepSeek adapter (dsh-base row `llm-deepseek`). Credential env is
# the default; per-model routing and reasoning defaults come from the
# `llm-deepseek:` section of profile/settings.yaml, never from this row.
- id: llm-deepseek
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-deepseek'
  config:
    apiKeyEnv: DEEPSEEK_API_KEY

# Local sandbox backend (dsh-base row `sandbox`). All config keys are optional
# and take their defaults; restated so the executor selection is explicit.
- id: sandbox
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-local'

# Sandbox policy (dsh-base row `sandbox-policy`). workspace-write lets the
# `coder` child mutate the workspace; the read-only presets (plan/build/
# explore/researcher/reviewer) are narrowed at runtime by the capability
# matrix (CAPABILITY_MATRIX + restrictPresetTools, dh-common) — they mount no
# bash/edit/write tool rows in their agent.cordis.yml and their matrix rows
# omit those names — not by the sandbox mode or any toolFilter key.
- id: sandbox-policy
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-policy'
  config:
    mode: !!js process.env.DSH_PERMISSION_MODE ?? 'workspace-write'
    workspaceRoot: !!js process.cwd()

# Session persistence (dsh-base row `session-persistence-jsonl`): JSONL
# backend rooted under $DSH_HOME/sessions (dshHomePath resolves $DSH_HOME,
# falling back to ~/.dsh). This is the session-persistence configuration.
- id: session-persistence-jsonl
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-persistence-jsonl'
  config:
    root: !!js dshHomePath('sessions')

# ── agent presets: provided by the SURFACE bundles ─────────────────────────

# The dsh-agent-presets service is NOT inserted here. The surface bundles own
# it: the dsh web app inserts its own `agent-presets` row, and the CLI appends
# its shipped preset root as the last overlay. We deliberately do NOT insert
# our own `agent-presets` row: a second bare insert collides with the web
# app's ("duplicate loader entry id"). Our presets are instead discovered
# through the USER root ($DSH_HOME/.agent-presets/), which includeUserRoot
# enables by default (dsh-agent-presets Config default true). dh-workspace's
# apply() mirrors the bundle's presets there at every boot
# (mirrorPresetsAtBoot, DESIGN.md §4). To change the default preset, set it in
# profile/settings.yaml:
#   agent-presets:
#     default: plan

# ── dh-multiagents plugins (row ids/names per DESIGN.md §2) ──────────────

- insert:
    - id: dh-workspace
      name: '@dh-multiagents/dh-workspace'
      # registers tools: plan_save, plan_read (+ systemPrompt.context sections)

    - id: dh-delegation
      name: '@dh-multiagents/dh-delegation'
      # registers tools: delegate, delegation_read, delegation_list

    - id: dh-subagent-preset
      name: '@dh-multiagents/dh-subagent-preset'
      # registers SubagentProvider names: explore, researcher, coder, scribe, reviewer

    - id: dh-worktree
      name: '@dh-multiagents/dh-worktree'
      # registers tools: worktree_create, worktree_delete

# Skills: dh-philosophy is a content package (NOT a plugin); its five
# SKILL.md files are surfaced through the skill-filesystem provider. The base
# row (dsh-base) carries no config; this override points bundledSkillDir at
# the skills dh-workspace mirrors into $DSH_HOME/.skills at every boot
# (mirrorSkillsAtBoot, DESIGN.md §5). dshHomePath is the same harness-home
# resolver the session-persistence row above uses, so the path survives a
# non-hoisted (pnpm-nested) install where a node_modules-relative lookup
# silently resolves to nothing.
- id: skill-filesystem
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem'
  config:
    bundledSkillDir: !!js dshHomePath('.skills')

readme.text: Multi-agent orchestration for the DeepSeek Harness (dsh). A team of role-bound agents — plan, build, explore, researcher, coder, scribe, reviewer — with tools enforced by a runtime capability matrix.

- **Plan-first** — read-only orchestrators delegate, never write code themselves.
- **Enforced, not suggested** — each preset's tool allow-list is applied via `tools.restrict`, so a plan agent physically can't run bash.
- **Auditable delegation** — every `delegate` call persists an id (e.g. `daring-pearl-elk`) with a result file on disk.
- **Zero-config install** — one command, presets + skills wired automatically.

Requires Node ≥ 22.19 and a dsh install (`@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.0-rc.6`).

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <name> init
dsh plugin --profile <name> add @dh-multiagents/bundle
```

> Presets are mirrored automatically at every boot (the plugin copies them
> into `$DSH_HOME/.agent-presets/`), so there is no install-time step.

> **Fresh dsh CLI (npm 11):** npm 11 blocks dependency install scripts by
> default — the harness's own native deps (`node-pty`, `dsh-subprocess-local`,
> `koffi`, `protobufjs`) are gated too. Run `npm install-scripts approve` for
> them before headless mode will boot.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Select `Plan` or `Build` at the start of your session:**
> In the Web or TUI interface, select either the **`plan`** or **`build`** preset in the preset picker at the beginning of your session:
> - **`plan`**: Use when starting a task to research the codebase and write an implementation plan (delegates to `explore` and `researcher`).
> - **`build`**: Use to execute an approved plan (delegates to `coder`, `scribe`, and `reviewer` with worktrees).
>
> Only `plan` and `build` act as orchestrators. The subagent presets (`explore`, `researcher`, `coder`, `scribe`, `reviewer`) are spawned automatically via `delegate` and should not be selected as top-level sessions.

readme.section: headless mode needs the headless bundle (add once)
readme.text:
dsh plugin --profile <name> add @deepseek-ai/dsh-headless

DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=... dsh --profile <name> headless \
  "Use plan_save to save a plan titled '# P' for project 'demo'. Then delegate '1+1?' to the researcher and report its answer."
```

For full orchestration (delegate/build), use the **tui** or **web** profile — headless sessions are preset-less by design, so `delegate` is rejected there (only `plan`/`build` presets may delegate).

| Preset | Role | Notable tools |
|---|---|---|
| `plan` | Read-only orchestrator | plan_save/read, delegate → explore/researcher |
| `build` | Read-only orchestrator | delegate → coder/scribe/reviewer, worktrees |
| `explore` | Codebase explorer | read, glob, grep |
| `researcher` | Web researcher | web_search, read |
| `coder` | Implementer | bash, edit, write, worktrees |
| `scribe` | Docs writer | edit, write, read |
| `reviewer` | Read-only reviewer | read, glob, grep |
Plus 5 philosophy skills (`code-philosophy`, `code-review`, `plan-review`, `plan-protocol`, `frontend-philosophy`) loaded into every session.

- Delegations persist as `$DSH_HOME/workspace/<project>/delegations/<id>.md` + `<id>.result.txt` — auditable after the fact.
- Only `plan`/`build` may delegate; plan → explore/researcher, build → +coder/scribe/reviewer. No delegation from inside a subagent (anti-recursion).
- Children inherit the parent's model selection.

```bash
pnpm install && pnpm -r build
```

- **Naming contract:** identifiers are locked in `DESIGN.md` — change it there first, never in code alone.
- **Presets/skills:** add `presets/<name>/` + a `CAPABILITY_MATRIX` entry (dh-common), or `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (dh-philosophy).
- **Publishing:** bump versions, then `pnpm pack` and publish the tarballs — plain `npm publish` leaves `workspace:*` unresolved (broke 0.1.0).
